71711-tales-out-of-school.title: Tales Out Of School
71711-tales-out-of-school.creator: Unknown
71711-tales-out-of-school.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. He had shot many a buffalo. Indeed he sometimes thought that he had shot too many, for out on our Western prairies it was often impossible for him to use the meat, or even to take the skins of the animals that fell before his generally unerring rifle. And the Colonel was very much opposed to the useless slaughter of wild animals.

arxiv-1512-06635.title: A Practically Efficient Algorithm for Generating Answers to Keyword Search over Data Graphs This work was supported by the Israel Science Foundation (Grant No. 1632/12). This paper is the full version of [ 5 ] .
arxiv-1512-06635.creator: Konstantin Golenberg, Yehoshua Sagiv
arxiv-1512-06635.description: Abstract In keyword search over a data graph, an answer is a non-redundant subtree that contains all the keywords of the query. A naive approach to producing all the answers by increasing height is to generalize Dijkstra’s algorithm to enumerating all acyclic paths by increasing weight.

arxiv-2005-14287.title: Mechanobiology predicts raft formations triggered by ligand-receptor activity across the cell membrane
arxiv-2005-14287.creator: A. R. Carotenuto, L. Lunghi, V. Piccolo, M. Babaei, K. Dayal, N. M. Pugno, M. Zingales, L. Deseri, M. Fraldi
arxiv-2005-14287.description: Abstract Clustering of ligand-binding receptors of different types on thickened isles of the cell membrane, namely lipid rafts, is an experimentally observed phenomenon. Although its influence on cell’s response is deeply investigated, the role of the coupling between mechanical processes and multiphysics involving the active receptors and the surrounding lipid membrane during ligand-binding has not yet been understood.

arxiv-2305-02957.title: A Monoidal View on Fixpoint Checks Thanks: Partially supported by the DFG project SpeQt (project number 434050016), by the Ministero dell’Universtà e della Ricerca Scientifica of Italy, under Grant No. 201784YSZ5, PRIN2017 – ASPRA, by project iNEST, No. J43C22000320006 and by the European Union - Ne
arxiv-2305-02957.creator: Paolo Baldan ORCID:0000-0001-9357-5599, Richard Eggert ORCID:0000-0002-9901-7392, Barbara König ORCID:0000-0002-4193-2889, Timo Matt ORCID:0009-0008-5570-6998, Tommaso Padoan ORCID:0000-0001-7814-1485
arxiv-2305-02957.description: Abstract . Fixpoints are ubiquitous in computer science as they play a central role in providing a meaning to recursive and cyclic definitions. Bisimilarity, behavioural metrics, termination probabilities for Markov chains and stochastic games are defined in terms of least or greatest fixpoints.

arxiv-2308-15879.title: Explanations for Answer Set Programming
arxiv-2308-15879.creator: Mario Alviano, Ly Ly Trieu & Tran Cao Son, Marcello Balduccini
arxiv-2308-15879.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mario Alviano, Ly Ly Trieu & Tran Cao Son, Marcello Balduccini. The paper presents an enhancement of 𝚡𝙰𝚂𝙿 \mathtt{xASP} , a system that generates explanation graphs for Answer Set Programming (ASP). Different from 𝚡𝙰𝚂𝙿 \mathtt{xASP} , the new system, 𝚡𝙰𝚂𝙿𝟸 \mathtt{xASP2} , supports different clingo constructs like the choice rules, the constraints, and the aggregates such as # ​ s ​ u ​ m \#sum , # ​ m ​ i ​ n \#min .

arxiv-2310-07398.title: Frequency mixing spectroscopy of spins in diamond
arxiv-2310-07398.creator: Mohammed Attrash, Sergei Masis, Sergey Hazanov, Oleg Shtempluck, Eyal Buks
arxiv-2310-07398.description: Abstract Frequency mixing processes in spin systems have a variety of applications in meteorology and in quantum data processing. Spin spectroscopy based on frequency mixing offers some advantages, including the ability to eliminate crosstalk between driving and detection. We experimentally explore nonlinear frequency mixing processes with negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy defects in diamond at low temperatures, and near level anti crossing.

arxiv-2406-06427.title: Notes on Kalman Filter (KF, EKF, ESKF, IEKF, IESKF)
arxiv-2406-06427.creator: Gyubeom Edward Im
arxiv-2406-06427.description: Abstract 1 Preliminaries The Kalman filter is an algorithm that recursively predicts and updates the state of a time-varying system based on the predictions of the system model and observations containing noise. This section provides a brief overview of the foundational knowledge before delving into the Kalman filter itself. 1.

arxiv-2409-09519.title: Nontrivial Kron Reduction for Power Grid Dynamics Modeling
arxiv-2409-09519.creator: Laurent Pagnier, IEEE Member, Robin Delabays, Melvyn Tyloo
arxiv-2409-09519.description: Abstract The Kron reduction is used in power grid modeling when the analysis can – supposedly – be restricted to a subset of nodes. Typically, when one is interested in the phases’ dynamics, it is common to reduce the load buses and focus on the generators’ behavior.

arxiv-2411-11553.title: Dynamical regimes of thermally convective emulsions
arxiv-2411-11553.creator: Francesca Pelusi, Andrea Scagliarini, Mauro Sbragaglia, Massimo Bernaschi, Roberto Benzi
arxiv-2411-11553.description: Abstract Emulsions are paramount in various interdisciplinary topical areas, yet a satisfactory understanding of their behavior in buoyancy-driven thermal flows has not been established. In the present work, we unravel the dynamical regimes of thermal convection in emulsions by leveraging a large set of mesoscale numerical simulations.

arxiv-2503-22090.title: Relatively non-degenerate integrated decay estimates on subextremal Kerr–de Sitter
arxiv-2503-22090.creator: Georgios Mavrogiannis
arxiv-2503-22090.description: Abstract . We study the Klein–Gordon equation □ ​ ψ − μ KG 2 ​ ψ = 0 \Box\psi-\mu^{2}_{\textit{KG}}\psi=0 on subextremal Kerr–de Sitter black hole backgrounds with parameters ( a , M , l ) (a,M,l) , where l 2 = 3 Λ l^{2}=\frac{3}{\Lambda} .

arxiv-2503-23202.title: Using Wavelet Decomposition to Determine the Dimension of Structures from Projected Images
arxiv-2503-23202.creator: Svitlana Mayboroda, David N Spergel
arxiv-2503-23202.description: Abstract Mesoscale structures can often be described as fractional dimensional across a wide range of scales. We consider a γ \gamma dimensional measure embedded in an N N dimensional space and discuss how to determine its dimension, both in N N dimensions and projected into D D dimensions.

arxiv-2504-19338.title: OpenFOAMGPT 2.0: end-to-end, trustworthy automation for computational fluid dynamics
arxiv-2504-19338.creator: Jingsen Feng, Ran Xu, Xu Chu
arxiv-2504-19338.description: Abstract We propose the first multi-agent framework for computational fluid dynamics that enables fully automated, end-to-end simulations directly from natural-language queries. The approach integrates four specialized agents—Pre-processing, Prompt Generation, OpenFOAMGPT (simulator), and Post-processing—decomposing complex computational fluid dynamics workflows into collaborative components powered by large language models.

arxiv-2507-12938.title: Unleashing Vision Foundation Models for Coronary Artery Segmentation: Parallel ViT-CNN Encoding and Variational Fusion
arxiv-2507-12938.creator: Caixia Dong, Duwei Dai, Xinyi Han, Fan Liu, Xu Yang, Zongfang Li (🖂), Songhua Xu (🖂)
arxiv-2507-12938.description: Abstract Accurate coronary artery segmentation is critical for computer-aided diagnosis of coronary artery disease (CAD), yet it remains challenging due to the small size, complex morphology, and low contrast with surrounding tissues. To address these challenges, we propose a novel segmentation framework that leverages the power of vision foundation models (VFMs) through a parallel encoding architecture.

arxiv-2509-18314.title: Exploiting Tree Structure for Credit Assignment in RL Training of LLMs
arxiv-2509-18314.creator: Hieu Tran, Zonghai Yao, Hong Yu
arxiv-2509-18314.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning improves LLM reasoning, yet sparse delayed reward over long sequences makes token-level credit assignment the key bottleneck. We study the verifiable-reward setting, where the final answer is checkable and multiple responses can be drawn per prompt. Reasoning tasks in math and medical QA align with this setup, where only a few decision tokens significantly impact the outcome.

arxiv-2509-25039.title: Effective Free Energy Landscapes and Hawking-Page Transitions
arxiv-2509-25039.creator: Choon-Lin Ho
arxiv-2509-25039.description: Abstract A recent interesting development on the dynamics of black hole phase transitions, the Hawking-Page transition, has been the so-called Gibbs free energy landscape approach. In this formalism, it is assumed that there exists a canonical ensemble of a series of black hole spacetimes with arbitrary horizon radius at a given ensemble temperature.

pmc-10753721.title: Influence of Anatomy, Microstructure, and Composition of Natural Fibers on the Performance of Thermal Insulation Panels
pmc-10753721.creator: Melek Ayadi, César Segovia, Ayda Baffoun, Riadh Zouari, Vanessa Fierro, Alain Celzard, Slah Msahli, Nicolas Brosse
pmc-10753721.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The growing interest in environmentally friendly materials is leading to a re-evaluation of natural fibers for industrial applications in order to meet sustainability and low-cost objectives, especially for thermal insulation of buildings. This paper deals with the chemical and physical characterization of fibers extracted from seagrass (Posidonia oceanica) and alfa grass (Stipa tenacissima) for a possible substitution of synthetic materials for thermal insulation. Hemp (Cannabis sativa), a fiber broadly used, was also studied for comparison.

pmc-11510059.title: Protective Role of Eicosapentaenoic and Docosahexaenoic and Their N-Ethanolamide Derivatives in Olfactory Glial Cells Affected by Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Neuroinflammation
pmc-11510059.creator: Rosalia Pellitteri, Valentina La Cognata, Cristina Russo, Angela Patti, Claudia Sanfilippo, Pierluigi Plastina
pmc-11510059.description: Neuroinflammation is a symptom of different neurodegenerative diseases, and growing interest is directed towards active drug development for the reduction of its negative effects. The anti-inflammatory activity of polyunsaturated fatty acids, eicosapentaenoic (EPA), docosahexaenoic (DHA), and their amide derivatives was largely investigated on some neural cells.

pmc-12593967.title: Biomimetic tri-layered osteochondral scaffold
pmc-12593967.creator: Manuela Salerno, Alessandro Di Martino, Elisabetta Galassi, Laura Grillini, Alessandro Dotti, Claudio De Luca, Giuseppe Filardo
pmc-12593967.description: AimsThe aim of this study was to investigate a biomimetic biodegradable cell-free osteochondral scaffold in a clinically relevant large animal model to quantify the early integration and regeneration phases after implantation.MethodsBilateral critical-sized osteochondral defects were created in 14 sheep. One defect was filled with the scaffold, whereas the contralateral was left empty.

pmc-12730618.title: A Patient-Derived Organoid Platform from TUR-P Samples Enables Precision Drug Screening in Advanced Prostate Cancer
pmc-12730618.creator: Zaukir Bostan Ali, Mooktapa Plikomol, Tanan Bejrananda, Paramee Thongsuksai, Pokphon Khirilak, Natthapon Khongcharoen, Karan Ulhaka, Ratsamaporn Nontikarn, Onpawee Phanthuvet, Pasarat Khongkow
pmc-12730618.description: Simple SummaryAdvanced prostate cancer (APC) is highly heterogeneous, often leading to treatment resistance. In this study, we optimized a cost-effective protocol to establish patient-derived organoids (PDOs) from transurethral resection of the prostate (TUR-P) samples, achieving a 62.07% success rate. These organoids preserved key features of the original tumors and enabled precise drug screening.

pmc-12957970.title: Altered Expression of GABA-Related Genes in Schizophrenia: Insights from Meta-Analyses of Brain and Blood Samples and iPSC-Derived Organoids
pmc-12957970.creator: Yuval Singer, Assif Yitzhaky, Libi Hertzberg
pmc-12957970.description: Background:Schizophrenia, one of the most disabling mental disorders, affects approximately seven per 1000 individuals worldwide and has an estimated heritability of around 80%; however, its pathophysiology remains incompletely understood. The disorder has been linked to dysregulation of multiple neurotransmitter systems, including dopamine, serotonin, γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA), and glutamate.

pmc-13378673.title: Perioperative Outcomes in Factor XI Deficiency: A Systematic Review
pmc-13378673.creator: Zainab Al‐Housni, Raeesah Mohammed, Silvio Ligia, Jim Douketis, Chatree Chai‐Adisaksopha, Alfonso Iorio, Davide Matino
pmc-13378673.description: BackgroundCongenital factor XI (FXI) deficiency has a variable bleeding phenotype, and FXI activity alone does not predict perioperative bleeding. Management practices remain heterogeneous, and available evidence derives from case reports, small case series, and retrospective cohorts. This systematic review evaluated perioperative bleeding outcomes and management strategies in FXI‐deficient patients undergoing surgical procedures.MethodsWe systematically searched five databases (2016–2024).

pmc-13444640.title: Tick-borne bacterial pathogens in wildlife and their parasitizing ticks in Korea: A molecular epidemiological study
pmc-13444640.creator: You-Jeong Lee, Beoul Kim, Yong Sun Hyun, Jae Woong Heo, Hyo-Min Woo, Jae-Woo Choi, Insu Choi, Yong‑Myung Kang, Man Hee Rhee, Dongmi Kwak, Kyoo-Tae Kim, Min-Goo Seo
pmc-13444640.description: Ticks are important vectors of numerous zoonotic pathogens, yet integrated molecular surveillance of wildlife hosts and their parasitizing ticks remains limited in Korea. In this study, we investigated the occurrence of major tick-borne bacterial pathogens in wildlife and their associated ticks.

pmc-13486691.title: The mediating role of sleep quality in the association between job stress and quality of life among medical university employees
pmc-13486691.creator: Zahra Hosseinkhani, Edris Kakemam, Maryam Hadji, Hassan Taherahmadi, Neda Mohammadi
pmc-13486691.description: Job stress is a risk factor for poor quality of life), but the mediating role of sleep quality is underexplored, particularly among medical university employees. This study examined the direct and indirect effects of job stress, measured using the effort-reward imbalance (ERI) model, on quality of life, with sleep quality as a hypothesized mediator.

pmc-13586847.title: Hydrangea medogensis (Hydrangeaceae), a new species from Xizang (Tibet), China
pmc-13586847.creator: Wen-Qi He, Wei-Lie Zheng, Fang-Yu Zhao, Kai-Xin Yin, Lian-Qiang Li, Kai-Hui Zhao, Fang-yuan Zhang, Zhi-hua Liao, Xiao-Zhong Lan
pmc-13586847.description: Based on field surveys, examination of herbarium specimens, and molecular phylogenetic analyses, the present study described a new species, Hydrangea medogensissp. nov. (Hydrangeaceae), from Medog County, Xizang Autonomous Region, China. Phylogenetic analyses indicated that H. medogensis was placed in Clade 1 as a distinct lineage, sister to the remainder of the clade.

pmc-13595137.title: Spatial-Frequency–Dependent Contrast Sensitivity in Early and Intermediate Age-Related Macular Degeneration
pmc-13595137.creator: Stefan Futterknecht, Maximilian Pfau, Ursula Hall, Chrysoula Gabrani, Philipp Anders, Georg Ansari, Ghislaine L Traber, Hendrik P Scholl, Nicolas Feltgen, Michael Herzog, Simona A Garobbio, Kristina Pfau
pmc-13595137.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate spatial-frequency–dependent differences in contrast sensitivity across early and intermediate age-related macular degeneration (eAMD and iAMD) and explore the discriminative value of visual function metrics beyond age.DesignCross-sectional observational study.SubjectsNinety-six participants from the Multimodal Assessment of Visual Function in Intermediate AMD study, including 49 controls, 14 participants with eAMD, and 33 with iAMD.

pmc-13664626.title: Hypoxia–ROS–HSP Triad Axis in Cancer: Mechanisms, Crosstalk, and Therapeutic Implications
pmc-13664626.creator: Manish Kumar Singh, Hyeong Rok Yun, Jyotsna Ranbhise, Sunhee Han, Seung Geun Yeo, Fu-Shi Quan, Bonglee Kim, Sung Soo Kim, Insug Kang
pmc-13664626.description: Highlights What are the main findings? This review highlights how three critical processes, namely, hypoxia, ROS, and heat shock proteins (HSPs), interplay in cancer establishment and survival.We demonstrate how diverse upstream stimuli and stressors within the tumor microenvironment converge upon common, progression-related signaling circuits through the synergistic interaction of this specific Hypoxia-ROS-HSP triad.
